note: Re-judged 2026-11-08 (independent auditor) after 10e9995d31 and 47f14d5ede moved DHCP serving into segment.serve (segment.go) and turned dhcpHandler.handle into a test shim (segment_test.go) that builds a one-subnet segment whose device holds serverAddr(h) and calls segment.serve, the same function serveRequests and serveMulti call (register.go). TestOverloadFieldsCarryOptions gained only a setup step: it reserves and binds the requested address for the client before sending the overloaded INIT-REBOOT, because segment.initReboot now stays silent for a client with no record (RFC 2131 Section 4.3.2). The assertions are unchanged: message type 53 and requested address 50 placed in file and/or sname under option 52 values 1, 2 and 3 must be found, and the request must draw a DHCPACK for that address. The binding does not make the positive pass without reading the overloaded fields: with 53 unread parseMsgType answers 0 and serve returns nil. The {partial} scope, its Tested and Gap spans and the client-side gap (internal/plugins/iface/dhcp/dhcp_v4_exchange_linux.go::acquire, nclient4 never consulting option 52) are unchanged, and records on options.go::findOption are current. Partial stands. Prior judgement: Rejudged 2026-10-30 (independent auditor) after the row gained a {partial} scope. RFC 2131 Section 4.1: "The options in the 'options' field MUST be interpreted first, so that any 'option overload' options may be interpreted." Tested: The options in the 'options' field MUST be interpreted first. Server: findOption walks the options field before file and sname; TestOverloadInterpretationOrder (positive, options copy wins under 52=3), TestOverloadFieldsCarryOptions (positive, 52 honoured) and the negative (a 52 inside file opens no sname) discriminate it, with revert records on every cover and the earlier overlay mutants. Client: FromBytes reads only the options field for options, so the order clause holds there too. Gap: so that any 'option overload' options may be interpreted. Producer internal/plugins/iface/dhcp/dhcp_v4_exchange_linux.go::acquire passes each reply to vendored nclient4, whose dhcpv4 FromBytes reads sname and file as strings and never consults option 52 (no build-time patch), so the client loses options a server places in an overloaded field.
